name: Madang (Malaysia)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired ISO code mqd, merged into Mainstream Kenyah [xkl] in 2008 (CR 2007-245); no Madang-specific description located.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Badeng data ('of the upper Baram River, Sarawak', 'Spoken at Lio' Mato') used in sec. 2.11.4 Kenyah and 3.2.1.1.1 (Kayan lexical influence in Badeng); all 20 occurrences of 'stress' concern Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh or areal remarks. No Kenyah/Badeng stress statement.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2008. The classification of Kenyah languages: A preliminary statement. Papers from SEALS XIV (2). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Badeng named only in the classification (Hudson's Kenyahic; shares lexical/phonological innovations with Ndang, Lepo' Ke', Bakung, Nyibun). No 'stress' in the text.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-245 (Karl Anderbeck, SIL Indonesia; adopted 2008-01-14): rename [xkl] Mainstream Kenyah; merge Madang [mqd] and Kenyah Bakung [boc] into it. 9 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Identity only: p.3 'According to Soriente (2005), Madang is another name of Badeng which is classified as Usun Apau Kenyah/Apo Kayan Kenyah/Mainstream Kenyah.. Group 3' (with Lepo Ma'ut, Lepo Ndang, Lepo Jamok).

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G. Jr. (ed.). 2005. Ethnologue, 15th ed., entry 'Madang' [mqd] (the Internet Archive 2006 capture).
sources.note: Nothing. Identity: 'Madang. A language of Malaysia (Sarawak). Population 2,222 (2000 WCD). Region Tinjar River, 4th Division. Alternate names Badang, Medang, Malang, Lepo Tau Kenyah, Lepo Tau Kenya, Lepu Tau. Classification.. North Sarawakan, Kenyah, Sebob.'

sources.citation: Eghenter, Cristina, Bernard Sellato & G. Simon Devung (eds.). 2003. Social science research and conservation management in the interior of Borneo. Bogor: CIFOR. (English adaptation of Eghenter & Sellato eds. 1999.)
sources.note: Nothing. Badeng appears only ethnographically (Pujungan Kenyah groups; Sellato's chapter cites Soriente 1999 for the grouping 'Leppu' Ndang, Bakung, Leppo' Ma'ut, Leppo' Ke, and Badeng'). Soriente's language chapter of the 1999 Indonesian original is not in this volume; 'stress' occurs only in non-linguistic senses.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 1999. Situasi kebahasaan di Kecamatan Long Pujungan. In Cristina Eghenter & Bernard Sellato (eds.), Kebudayaan dan pelestarian alam: Penelitian interdisipliner di pedalaman Kalimantan, 465-483. Jakarta: WWF Indonesia / PHPA / Ford Foundation.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 1997. The Kenyah isolects of Long Pujungan District in North-East Kalimantan. In Cecilia Ode & Wim Stokhof (eds.), Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, 713-738. Amsterdam: Rodopi (Brill reissue 2023).
